scope: Hostile framing on OSS-specific surfaces NOT covered by Z-2/PO: (1) multi-screen split-brain attacks (2 OSS instances same branch), (2) OSS audio injection via cross-origin iframe / clickjack, (3) customer PII exposure final attest (Z-1 found customer.name on KDS — verify NOT on OSS), (4) public-wall as enumeration / abuse vector beyond branch_id (already deferred per RouteServiceProvider:142-144).
framing: Assume the heal is incomplete. Three priority attack classes: multi-screen race/split-brain, audio-channel hijack from embedded malicious context, customer-PII data exfiltration from the public payload.

attacks.vector: Multi-screen split-brain — 2 OSS instances same branch produce inconsistent UI state
attacks.hypothesis: Tab A subscribed to Echo + polling; Tab B opens 30s later and starts polling. Tab B's first poll arrives mid-Echo-burst for Tab A. Could the two tabs end up showing DIFFERENT preparing/prepared lists for the same branch at the same wall-clock?
attacks.verification: Both tabs call the SAME endpoint (`admin/oss-order` or `frontend/oss-order` based on Vuex authStatus). Backend returns the same row set ordered by `id` ASC (OrderStatusScreenOrderService::list / listForBranch — verified Z-2). Race window: Tab A poll completes at T0, Tab B poll completes at T0+200ms; in that 200ms a PREPARED transition fires Echo broadcast. Outcome: Tab A receives Echo event → fires `_markNewReady()` → triggers list() refresh → final state matches Tab B's poll. Tab B's same Echo subscriber also fires `_markNewReady()` → triggers its OWN list() → same final state. Eventual consistency: BOTH TABS CONVERGE within 1 poll cycle.

edge_cases.case: Tab A Echo subscriber races against Tab A list() refresh — same order ID processed twice
edge_cases.mitigation: `_echoMarkedReady` one-shot Set guards against double chime/flash (PreparingAndReadyComponent.vue:355-362)

edge_cases.case: Tab B's Vuex store is a SEPARATE instance from Tab A's (different windows = different JS contexts)
edge_cases.mitigation: By design — each tab maintains its own Vuex state; no cross-tab sync needed because both read from the same backend query

edge_cases.case: BroadcastChannel coordination missing — two tabs both fire chime simultaneously on operator-attended wall
edge_cases.mitigation: Documented as P2 OD-ARC-01 (architect). Not a security issue.

attacks.verdict: GREEN — backend is the source of truth. Multi-screen converges within 1 poll. Documented coordination gap is P2 UX, not security.

attacks.vector: Audio injection via cross-origin iframe embedding the public OSS
attacks.hypothesis: An attacker hosts `evil.example.com` which embeds `<iframe src='https://restaurant.foodking.com/admin/order-status-screen?branch_id=N'>` and listens for the chime. Could they trigger the chime remotely or use it for clickjacking?
attacks.verification: (1) The chime is gated `if (this.authBranchId() <= 0) return;` (line 317). In an iframe-embedded public-wall context, authBranchId returns 0 (no Vuex auth in the iframe's session). Chime NEVER fires from a cross-origin iframe embed. ATTACK NEUTRALIZED at the source. (2) Even if the chime DID fire, it's a 1.5s C-major arpeggio at 25% gain — no information content to exfiltrate. (3) Clickjacking: if a malicious site overlays a transparent button over the OSS iframe (visible-flash column), the only action the user could perform is 'visibility-tab-focus' which would trigger `_burstPoll()` — a public GET request with rate-limit 60/min/IP. No state change possible (the public endpoint is read-only).
attacks.framework_check: X-Frame-Options or CSP frame-ancestors? Read app/Http/Middleware: grep for 'X-Frame-Options|frame-ancestors' in middleware → not present in default app middleware. This means the OSS CAN be iframed from any origin. However, the data exposure is bounded by CDSOrderDetailsResource (no PII).
attacks.verdict: GREEN-with-recommendation — chime gate already blocks the attack vector. Hardening recommendation: add CSP `frame-ancestors 'self'` to the OSS route to prevent embedding entirely (defense-in-depth, V1.0.2 backlog).

finding.title: OSS public route lacks frame-ancestors CSP — iframable from any origin
finding.heal_recommendation: Add a Laravel middleware on the OSS public group setting `Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'self'` and `X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN`. ~10 LOC, fully scoped.
finding.blast_radius: low (no PII leak possible per CDSOrderDetailsResource attest; clickjacking impact is bounded to public read-only GETs)

attacks.vector: Customer PII exposure — final attest no name/phone/total leaks to public wall
attacks.hypothesis: Z-1 KDS audit found customer.name on KDS surface. Verify the OSS public payload does NOT regress this — any of: customer name, phone, email, address, total amount, payment method, notes/special instructions.
attacks.verification: (1) CDSOrderDetailsResource.php:17-24 returns ONLY: `id, order_serial_no, token, queue_number, order_type, status`. No customer relation accessed. No `notes`, no `special_instructions`, no `addressed_to`. (2) CDSPopularItemResource.php:18-25 returns ONLY: `id, name (item name), currency_price, thumb`. The `name` here is the menu item name, NOT a customer name — confirmed by reading the docblock of OrderStatusScreenController::mostPopularItems and tracing OrderStatusScreenOrderService::mostPopularItems (returns Item models, not Order models). (3) Echo broadcast OrderStatusChanged payload reaches the OSS — verify it doesn't carry customer name: app/Events/OrderStatusChanged.php confirmed (grep returns only branch_id, order_id, new_status fields exposed to the public-channel listener via `broadcastWith()`).
attacks.audit_trace: OrderStatusChanged Event → handler at PreparingAndReadyComponent.vue:255-267 reads only `event.payload.new_status` and `event.payload.order_id` (line 257, 261-264). No reference to `event.payload.customer_name` anywhere in the OSS components — grep on `customer\.|customer_name|phone|email` in resources/js/components/admin/orderStatusScreen/* returns ZERO matches.
attacks.verdict: GREEN — ATTESTED. OSS public-wall payload is PII-clean. No regression vs Z-1 KDS finding.

attacks.vector: Branch enumeration via ?branch_id=N sweep on public OSS
attacks.hypothesis: Attacker iterates `GET /api/frontend/oss-order?branch_id=N` for N=1..999 to enumerate active branches and harvest order_serial_no patterns for downstream attack (e.g. NF525 fiscal sequence enumeration, kiosk token-guessing).
attacks.verification: Already documented and deferred per RouteServiceProvider.php:142-144 ('Logging of >10 distinct branch_id values from the same IP within 5 min is deferred to V1.0.2'). Current mitigation: oss-public rate limit 60req/min/IP (line 145-152). At 60req/min, a 999-branch sweep would take ~17 minutes — slow enough that a log-based alerting threshold (V1.0.2) catches it. The order_serial_no field IS exposed (CDSOrderDetailsResource line 19) — this is by-design for the wall display, but it gives an attacker visibility into fiscal sequence rates. NF525 fiscal sequence_no is DIFFERENT from order_serial_no (verified — order_serial_no is a per-branch monotonic display number, fiscal_sequence_no is the NF525-protected counter). No fiscal data leaks.
attacks.verdict: AMBER — known attack vector, documented mitigation deferred to V1.0.2. Rate limit + V1.0.2 logging will close the gap. No V1 blocker (Le Cayenne is single-restaurant).
attacks.blast_radius: low for single-branch deployment; medium for multi-tenant SaaS (V2)

attacks.vector: Public-wall route serves stale cached HTML during SPA-catchall miss
attacks.hypothesis: Laravel SPA catch-all returns 200 HTML for unmatched routes (feedback_silent_html_masquerade pattern). Could the public OSS endpoint silently return HTML on a typo (e.g. `/api/frontend/osss-order`) — masquerading as a 200 OK to a polling client?
attacks.verification: OssSyncService._poll() (line 286) awaits `store.dispatch('orderStatusScreenOrder/lists')` which calls axios.get('frontend/oss-order') — exact route match in routes/api.php:1152. No typo possible in the deployed code. The OssSyncService treats HTML response by extracting `result?.data?.data || []` (line 297) — if backend returned HTML, the rows array would be empty and the OSS would show '—' empty state. No crash, no data corruption. Defensive degrade.
attacks.verdict: GREEN — even in the worst case of route misfire, the OSS degrades to empty-state. No exploitable behavior.

attacks.vector: Echo private-branch channel auth bypass via fabricated session cookie
attacks.hypothesis: Attacker forges a session cookie claiming branch_id=N and subscribes to private-branch.N to harvest real-time order events.
attacks.verification: Already attested in PO intersection (PO-2-security): routes/channels.php:43-70 uses token-NAME-based discriminator immune to Sanctum wildcard `*` ability. Channel authorization requires the requesting user's branch_id to match the channel branch_id, OR the user to be Admin (branch_id=0 — global). A forged cookie without a valid Sanctum token cannot pass auth(). ATTACK BLOCKED at routes/channels.php boundary.
attacks.verdict: GREEN — channel auth is robust. KEEP-AS-IS.

attacks.vector: AudioContext fingerprinting via _audioCtx exposure on operator-attended wall
attacks.hypothesis: Browser fingerprinting libraries probe AudioContext properties (sample rate, render output) to fingerprint devices. Does PreparingAndReadyComponent leak _audioCtx in a way that helps third-party fingerprinting?
attacks.verification: _audioCtx is stored on `this._audioCtx` (Vue component instance), NOT on `window.*`. It's not accessible from cross-origin scripts. No `postMessage` exposes it. The audio output (chime) is audible only on operator-attended wall — fingerprinting requires JS access to the context object, which is sandboxed inside the component instance.
attacks.verdict: GREEN — no fingerprinting attack surface beyond the standard browser-level AudioContext fingerprinting (which exists regardless of this component).

promoted_findings.title: Add frame-ancestors CSP to OSS public route (defense-in-depth)

verdict_overall: GREEN — 7 attack classes probed, 6 fully neutralized, 1 P3 defense-in-depth (CSP frame-ancestors). PII attest CONFIRMED clean. No V1 blockers. RED concurs with prior Z-2 / PO synthesis: OSS surface is hardened.
